fair_value_reason: All agents now use net cash of $2.0-2.1B and the corrected Trainium4 and warrant facts, so no factual correction remains. Revised fair values are $338 / $352 / $356 / $349 and differ only on the multiple (40-45x NTM EPS of $8.0-8.6). I keep their mean, about $349, about 2% below spot.

thesis_triggers.event: The four agents give $205-212, all at about 32-33x 2027 consensus EPS of $6.39. Below about $208 the market would be pricing the loss of the ~$3B 2027 revenue path: a lost or double-sourced AWS scale-up socket, a Q4 guide at or below the ~$550M Q3 level, or real hyperscaler capex cuts rather than Fed or AI-sentiment swings.

supervisor_summary: The four revised forecasts took up every round-1 finding and converged: fair values $338-356 (mean ~$349, just under the $357.84 spot), thesis breaks $205-212, and a median at about spot. That convergence largely reflects shared supervisor inputs rather than new independent evidence. The remaining gap is a 40x-vs-45x multiple judgment that search cannot settle. I keep the mean ladder except for a slightly fatter far-left tail to cover the missing skeptic lane; confidence is low. The next real information is the Q3 print and Q4 guide around Nov 3-5, just after the one-month window.
key_drivers: Q3 2026 guide $540-560M (+40% q/q) and EPS $1.16-1.21; the Q3 print and Q4 guide (~Nov 3-5, Q4 consensus about $655M) are the first hard test of the Scorpio X ramp.
Valuation: about 56x 2027 consensus EPS $6.39. The one-year outcome hinges on whether the multiple compresses to about 40x (agent_2) or 44-45x (others) as growth slows toward 30%.
Concentration: top-3 customers are 69% of Q2 revenue. AWS ties are formalised by a warrant vesting on up to $6.5B of cumulative purchases through 2033, which is a ceiling, not a backlog.
Scale-up fabric competition: UALink (native Trainium4 racks, an ALAB opportunity) versus NVLink Fusion hybrid racks and Broadcom scale-up Ethernet.
Macro and sentiment: a Fed hike about 70% priced for Oct 28 and OpenAI's widened training pause, against no hyperscaler capex cuts so far.
